# hivelocity_null_route (Resource)

Null-routes (blackholes) one of your IP addresses at the network edge, for example to stop an incoming DDoS. Destroying the resource removes the null route. The resource ID is the IP address.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hivelocity_null_route" "under_attack" {
  ip      = "66.165.231.122"
  comment = "Mitigating volumetric attack, ticket 12345"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip` (String) IP address to null-route.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form note explaining why the address is null-routed.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `admin_id` (Number) ID of the admin who created the route, if created by Hivelocity staff.
- `client_id` (Number) Owning client ID.
- `created` (String) When the null route was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the IP address
terraform import hivelocity_null_route.under_attack 66.165.231.122
```
